key_insight: Apparent forgetting in continually trained language models depends on the evaluation interface and can reflect head–backbone mismatch rather than complete loss of learned representations.
engineering_relevance: For engineering language-model workflows updated across tasks, separating readout failure from representation drift could guide more targeted repairs, though solid-mechanics applications were not evaluated.
method: Compare the sequentially trained head, a fresh probe on frozen backbone features, and classifier-free backbone diagnostics.
Measure interface-dependent backward and forward transfer across incremental-learning settings.
Apply Just LM-Head Tuning (JLT) while keeping the incrementally trained backbone fixed.
evidence_signal: Across encoder and decoder backbones, class-incremental experiments and task-incremental checks showed interface-dependent forgetting; JLT recovered 96–99% of the gap to joint training for replay- and distillation-based methods, versus about three quarters for plain sequential fine-tuning.
watch_item: High recoverability with a newly trained readout does not imply preserved deployed performance or eliminate partial representation drift.
paper_title: Revisiting Continual Learning in Language Models: A Three-Interface Diagnosis of Stability and Plasticity
